changelog: First public release of fx-garages — server-authoritative garage system with in-game editor, real parking and vehicle showroom (QBCore / Qbox / ESX Legacy).

NEW — a garage can now be deleted from the /garagedev panel. Every garage in the Nearby list has a Sil button next to Duzenle; the first click turns it into Onayla / Vazgec, so a misclick cannot remove a garage. The delete itself was already fully built on the server side — permission re-check, revision guard, audit trail and live sync were all there — but the panel had no button and no way to send that intent, so deleting a garage meant typing /garagedev delete <id> and knowing the id. Pressing Escape cancels a pending confirmation, and the editor session stays open afterwards so several garages can be removed one after another.

Fixed the map blip of a deleted garage staying on every player's map until they reconnected. The removal was broadcast as a zone delta, and a zone delta only reaches players inside the roughly 225 m subscription window — but blips are map-wide and are fetched once and then held on the client, so everyone further away kept seeing a blip for a garage that no longer existed. Deletion is now announced to all players separately. The announcement carries a single garage id and the client drops just that one blip, so it does not make every player re-request the whole blip index.

What happens on delete is unchanged and still follows Config.GarageDev.allowHardDelete. Left at the default false, the garage is switched off rather than erased, so the vehicles stored there keep their garage_id and the change can be undone; set to true the row is deleted, but only when the garage holds no stored vehicles — otherwise the request is refused instead of quietly losing the vehicles. Either way the garage, its markers and its blip disappear for everyone immediately, with no restart.

Dropped the experimental use_experimental_fxv2_oal flag from fxmanifest.lua. It swapped Lua's native calls for an experimental faster path, and FiveM still labels that path experimental: it changes the return types of natives and breaks on any native whose declared argument types are wrong. The resource now runs on the same standard Lua runtime as every other resource, which is the safer place to be for the small amount of native-call time it costs back. Nothing in the resource depended on it.

UPGRADING: locales/*.json is escrow_ignored, so your own translation files are kept and will not contain the new notice_disable_ok line. Nothing breaks without it — the message falls back to notice_delete_ok, which you already have. Copy the new line over from the shipped locale file if you want the disabled case worded separately from the deleted one.
